arena.name: decision-arena
arena.title: Decision Arena
arena.question: For bounded classification (pick a label, yes/no, a score), should a decision model like Jev make the call, or a cheap LLM?

headline: Use **jev-1.14** (99% accurate, 185ms median, $0.0183 per 1k calls). Best decision model (jev-1.14, 99%) vs best LLM (haiku-5.5, 98%): no significant accuracy difference; the decision model is 7.7× faster and 3.3× cheaper.

pick.name: jev-1.14
pick.reason: Best combined cost and speed among models within 2 points of the top and not significantly worse (99% accurate, 185ms median, $0.0183 per 1k calls).

labels.note: About 120 hand-labeled examples; enough to spot differences between models, not to rank close ones.

data.description: 119 examples across 8 bounded decision tasks (lead relevance, entity resolution, page type, ticket urgency, ...), tagged by scenario.

method.rules: Tied = within 2% of the top accuracy and not significantly worse (exact McNemar, p < 0.05); pick = best combined cost and latency rank among tied. Pooled over every dataset; failed calls count as wrong.

outcome.note: Not yet recorded which enable-ai decisions moved because of this result.

caveats: Most models score 95%+ on these datasets, so the pick is driven by cost and speed; harder or real examples are needed to separate them on quality.
Treat a 1-2 point accuracy gap as noise at this sample size.
LLM reasoning is turned off where possible so latency comparisons are fair.
